title: PGGT-Loc: Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer for Feed-Forward Camera Localization
claim: Prior localizers need multi-step, map-specific pipelines; ours uses one feed-forward transformer that handles different map types.
layout: 3 panels: prior methods left stacked, ours right; color-coded blue/orange tracks
description: The figure has three parts. Panels (a) PlanaReLoc (blue) and (b) SPVLoc (orange) sit on the left, each as a three-step numbered pipeline with small illustrations. (a) shows plane recovery, primitive matching with lines between planes, and robust pose estimation. (b) shows panoramic map rendering, retrieval and viewpoint matching, and relative pose regression. Panel (c), "Ours: PGGT-Loc", takes up the right and centre. It has two parallel tracks. A blue track takes a query image and a 3D surface map. An orange track takes a query image and a layout model. Both tracks patchify the image and convert the map into primitive tiles. Both feed one central gradient-filled "Primitive-Grounded Geo. Transformer" box, which outputs a camera pose arrow in the 3D scene or floor plan. The eye goes first to the central transformer box.
caption: Overview. (a) PlanaReLoc [90] localizes cameras against dense surface maps by explicitly matching 2D plane proposals with planar map primitives. (b) SPVLoc [25] localizes cameras against minimal layout models by retrieving the best-matching panoramic rendering. (c) Our PGGT-Loc operates directly on query patches and map primitives, enabling feed-forward localization across both dense surface maps and minimal layout models with a unified base architecture.
abstract: Camera localization methods are mostly multi-stage pipelines relying on dedicated and complex maps that are costly to construct, store, and maintain over time. Alternatively, well-structured maps that organize scenes with compact yet expressive primitives are often readily available, providing rich structural and semantic cues that humans can interpret. However, their potential for direct camera localization remains largely unexplored due to the significant modality gap between map primitives and visual observations. This motivates a new concept for localization, which estimates camera poses by grounding query observations to map primitives. In this paper, we instantiate the concept in the context of planar primitives with PGGT, the Primitive-Grounded Geometry Transformer network. Given a single query image and a set of planar map primitives, the network is trained to predict multiple localization targets for feed-forward 6-DoF camera localization that generalizes to unseen environments. With this straightforward and scalable architecture, our method pushes the state-of-the-art localization performance on both dense surface maps and minimal layout models. The code and models are available at https://github.com/3dv-casia/PGGT-Loc
